label: High-Distress Heavy-Screen-Time Graduate Women
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who spend more than five hours daily on screens and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness score (1.73), PHQ-9 depression score (1.73), and GAD-7 anxiety score (2.13) all sit in the higher range, indicating a consistent pattern of psychological distress across all three dimensions, with anxiety being the most pronounced.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen time exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Reports elevated loneliness consistent with reduced meaningful social connection
Endorses moderate-to-high depressive symptoms including low mood and diminished interest
Exhibits the highest distress on anxiety measures, suggesting persistent worry and tension
Engages in prolonged daily screen use (>5 hours), which may both reflect and reinforce social withdrawal
Represents a sizeable subgroup (n=184), indicating this distress pattern is not uncommon among educated women with heavy screen habits
tone: Concerned and empathetic, acknowledging significant co-occurring psychological burdens

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With UCLA-8 loneliness, PHQ-9 depression, and GAD-7 anxiety scores all well below scale midpoints, these individuals appear to be psychologically well-adjusted and emotionally stable. They spend a moderate amount of time (1–3 hours) on the activities measured, suggesting balanced engagement rather than excessive or minimal use.
demographic_anchor: Male, holding a graduate degree or above, with 1–3 hours of daily usage
behavior_markers: Reports very low loneliness levels (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.72 on normalized scale)
Maintains moderate daily usage of 1–3 hours, suggesting balanced engagement
Belongs to a relatively well-represented cluster (n = 113 in training split)

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report consistently low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With mean scores well below clinical thresholds on all three validated scales (UCLA-8 loneliness ≈ 1.21, PHQ-9 depression ≈ 0.78, GAD-7 anxiety ≈ 0.79), these individuals demonstrate strong psychological well-being across emotional and social dimensions.
demographic_anchor: Male, holding a graduate degree or above, with moderate daily screen/internet usage of 1–3 hours
behavior_markers: Reports minimal feelings of social isolation or loneliness
Maintains moderate and controlled screen time (1–3 hours daily)
Scores consistently below clinical concern thresholds across all three mental health measures
tone: Stable, emotionally resilient, and socially connected
